payload.task_text:
I am building a knowledge base for our university and need to create a structured course catalog from the learning management system data. Please look up all courses from the Fall 2014 semester, which are the ones with course codes ending in 2014J.

For each course, I need the course name, course code, the start date and end date, the total number of enrolled students (count only enrollments of type StudentEnrollment, including all enrollment states such as active and completed; exclude teachers and teaching assistants), the number of assignments, and the list of instructors (users enrolled with a TeacherEnrollment in the course) with their names and email addresses.

Create a page in our knowledge base wiki for each course. The page title should be "[Course Code] - [Course Name]". The page content should include the following information as text: the course code, the semester (Fall 2014), the start and end dates in YYYY-MM-DD format, the student enrollment count (StudentEnrollment type, all states such as active and completed), the number of assignments, and a list of all instructors with their names and emails. Create the pages in alphabetical order by course code.

Also create an Excel file called course_catalog.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Courses" with columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Start_Date (YYYY-MM-DD format), End_Date (YYYY-MM-DD format), Student_Count, Assignment_Count, and Instructor_Names (a comma-separated list of instructor names sorted alphabetically). Sort rows by Course_Code alphabetically. The second sheet should be called "Summary" with a two-column layout where column A has labels and column B has values. The rows should be Total_Courses, Total_Students (sum of all student counts across courses), Total_Assignments (sum of all assignment counts), Largest_Course (the course code with the most students), Smallest_Course (the course code with the fewest students), and Most_Assignments (the course code with the most assignments).

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent performs the bounded seven-course source work directly, then uses one parallel writer wave. Canvas is read-only. Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically and freeze the exact Fall 2014 mapping returned by canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true): IDs 2,4,7,10,14,17,21 with their course codes and full Canvas names.

For all seven courses, issue ready calls in native-parallel batches: canvas_list_assignments once per course, canvas_get_course_grades(page=1,per_page=100,type=["StudentEnrollment"]) and the same for TeacherEnrollment, and canvas_list_course_users once per course. Student_Count comes from StudentEnrollment pagination.total_count. Teacher rows fit the returned page; if pagination says otherwise, follow it. When a roster result is oversized, read its complete full_output_path rather than the truncated preview. Join each TeacherEnrollment user_id only to its course roster, deduplicate by literal enrollment row.id, and sort instructor names alphabetically. Freeze seven code-sorted rows with exact full name, YYYY-MM-DD start/end, StudentEnrollment count, assignment count, and every instructor name/email, plus the six requested Summary metrics. Do not dispatch source or aggregation agents.

Wave 1 — start two Coder writers in parallel from that frozen table:

1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of course_catalog.xlsx: create exactly Courses and Summary with the task's exact headers/row order and literal values, then read both complete ranges back.
2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole Notion owner for the seven titles `[Course Code] - [Course Name]`. For each title, exhaust `API-post-search`, filter exact matches, create at most once on zero with `API-post-page(parent={"workspace":true}, properties={"title":{"title":[{"type":"text","text":{"content":<exact title>}}]}}, children=[<canonical paragraph block>])`, reuse one retained page, and block on multiple matches or an ambiguous create. For a reused page, retrieve it and use `API-patch-block-children` only to add a missing canonical paragraph. The paragraph contains code, Fall 2014, dates, StudentEnrollment count, assignment count, and all instructor names/emails. Search the title again, require exactly the retained ID, and read its complete child-block text back.

Each writer self-corrects before returning. The main agent reconciles exact seven-code/full-name coverage, counts and instructor identities across the external workbook and Notion read-backs. No second wave or audit agent is allowed.

You are working with a MOCK Notion server (fastmcp-based) via mcp__notion__* tools. The workspace is empty (API-post-search returns no results). Your job: create Notion wiki pages for a university course catalog for the Fall 2014 semester.

## Background / known issues (from my testing)
- `mcp__notion__API-create-a-comment` works fine with plain JSON object parameters (even with a fake page_id).
- `mcp__notion__API-patch-block-children` works and CAN create blocks of type "child_page" (they get real ids), but those are NOT indexed as pages: API-post-search does not find them and API-retrieve-a-page returns null for them.
- `mcp__notion__API-post-page` — the ONLY tool that creates real pages — currently fails argument validation in MY session for every parent shape I tried. The error is always exactly: `Invalid args for tool "mcp__notion__API-post-page": /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must match exactly one schema in oneOf`. Shapes I already tried (all failed):
  1. {"workspace": true, "type": "workspace"}
  2. {"workspace": true}
  3. {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true}
  4. {"page_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}
  5. {"type": "page_id", "page_id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"}
  In YOUR session the validation might behave differently — test it first before anything else.

## Step 1 — attempt real page creation
Try `mcp__notion__API-post-page` to create a top-level page titled "Fall 2014 Course Catalog" with parent {"type": "workspace", "workspace": true} and properties {"title": [{"text": {"content": "Fall 2014 Course Catalog"}}]}. If validation fails, try a few reasonable parent variants (e.g., {"workspace": true}; page_id form against the anchor block id 8eed1b49-9b4c-464f-882c-6b6ee613ddc0; also try omitting optional params, or a minimal properties object). Do NOT spend more than ~6 attempts total. Record which variant, if any, passes.

IF a variant passes: create these pages exactly as specified below (parent page "Fall 2014 Course Catalog" created under workspace; the 7 course pages as children of it, in this exact order — alphabetical by course code). Verify afterwards with API-post-search (e.g., query "2014J") and/or API-retrieve-a-page, and report the page ids.

IF no variant passes: skip to the fallback section.

## Fallback (only if post-page validation never passes)

Then for each created child_page block id, append its content blocks via API-patch-block-children (block_id = the new child page's block id). Report every created block id.
